hypothesis: A compact global-attention model with observed-reference velocity features and learned residual confidence will improve long-range motion while leaving easy short-gap procedural references undisturbed more reliably than the local temporal convolution.
controlled_changes: Replace the six-block dilated temporal convolution with a four-block, four-head, width-128 Transformer encoder.
Append signed-log finite-difference velocity of the observed-only procedural baseline to each condition row.
Predict a per-frame confidence gate and regularize residual magnitude and gate activation so the model can retain a strong procedural reference.
held_constant: The 153-channel semantic pose, original 394 observed-only condition channels, exact strongest shape reference and C2 residual envelope.
The 1,840-clip, 85-subject, 7.158742-hour train split, subject-balanced sampler, two fixed seeds, gap/context/pattern cycle and 48,000 examples per seed.
AdamW settings, direct position/rotation/velocity/acceleration loss terms, protected development controls and all original acceptance gates.
No style conditioning, diffusion, runtime promotion or confirmation access in this experiment.

data.sampling: Subject uniform, then clip uniform within subject, then start uniform within clip. Gap/context balanced by deterministic step cycle; patterns 0,1,2 balanced within each batch.
data.window_materialization: Current batch only from memory-mapped positions and precomputed rotation matrices.

training.loss: unknown position MSE + 0.1 rotation6 MSE + 0.01 velocity MSE + 0.0001 acceleration MSE using actual seconds + residual/gate regularization
training.selection: Fixed final step only; no development checkpoint selection

evaluation.confirmation: All protected confirmation clips remain sealed unless both seeds pass every development gate.
